name: East Lothian Council
ownership_summary: Local authority; bought the ~92 ha former Cockenzie power station site from ScottishPower in 2018. Would lease ~70 acres of the coal store to a joint venture with SDCL, with no capital contribution; equity/revenue return to the council not yet finalised.
notes: Also the planning authority for any future application — a dual role (landowner/JV partner and decision-maker) noted by local commentators.

name: Sustainable Development Capital LLP (SDCL)
ownership_summary: Investment firm founded 2007 by Jonathan Maxwell (founder and CEO); specialises in energy efficiency and decentralised energy infrastructure; acts as developer, investor and fund manager; manages the listed SDCL Energy Efficiency Income Trust (SEIT). London HQ with offices in New York, Greenwich, Dublin, Hong Kong and Singapore.
notes: Selected as preferred bidder via competitive tender agreed in a private report to Council, February 2025; announced 22 October 2025. Prospective joint-venture partner rather than confirmed applicant; end operator not identified.

name: Cockenzie and Port Seton Community Council
notes: Chair Ben Morse has called for residents to be able to 'properly scrutinise' the joint venture before any planning application.

name: Prestonpans Community Council
notes: Raised concerns including 'greenwashing' of environmental claims, unclear water usage, absent community-benefits framework, and fear of minimal local job creation.
